findings.problem: scenario-panel.md (slice 18 test contract) says the `mat-stroked-button` is `custom-wildcard-add` and the `mat-icon-button` is `custom-wildcard-remove-<i>` (aria-label "Remove <label>"). The code puts `data-testid="custom-wildcard-add"` on an inner <span> and `custom-wildcard-remove-<i>` on the <mat-icon>, not on the buttons. Every other button in the app (generate-button, recent-futures-button, recent-future-<id>) has the testid on the <button>. As a result, getByTestId(...) toBeEnabled / toHaveAttribute('aria-label') / focus checks point at a non-interactive element. The unit tests only pass because they work around it with .closest('button').
findings.fix: Move `data-testid="custom-wildcard-add"` onto the <button mat-stroked-button> and `[attr.data-testid]="'custom-wildcard-remove-' + i"` onto the <button mat-icon-button>. The existing .closest('button') calls in the tests still work because closest() also matches the element itself.

findings.problem: The backend trims with String.strip() (Character.isWhitespace), but the UI trims with JS String.trim(). The two disagree on U+00A0 (NBSP), U+FEFF and U+2007/U+202F. A direct API call with label "\u00A0" is accepted as a 1-character label, while the UI would reject the same input as blank. This cannot happen through the panel, which sends labels already trimmed.
findings.fix: Trim with the same whitespace set as JS trim(), e.g. a regex on ^[\s\u00A0\uFEFF\p{Z}]+|...$, or treat Character.isSpaceChar as whitespace too.

findings.problem: The error is a plain role="alert" <div> outside the mat-form-field. The input has no aria-describedby / aria-invalid pointing to it, and the field does not show Material's error styling. Screen readers do announce the alert, but the error is not tied to the field.
findings.fix: Render the message as <mat-error> inside the form field (with a matching error state), or add [attr.aria-invalid] and aria-describedby that point to the error element.
